correctness.rationale: Contracting the c-antidiagonal matching gives the interval [0,c] with exactly the edges of lengths d=c-b and e=c-a. The contracted graph has the same cycle rank. Put N=c+1 and g=gcd(d,e)=gcd(b-a,d). At the Fine–Wilf threshold N0=d+e-g each residue modulo g is connected, and there are N0-g edges, so the threshold graph is a forest. Shorter intervals induce subgraphs of it; longer intervals have g components and (N-d)+(N-e) edges. This proves the rank max(0,N-d-e+g)=max(0,a+1-d+g) and the strict forest boundary a<d-g. In particular this includes the equality boundary, d=1, and g=d. Cycles persist under extension. Appending t=2m+1 after maximum sum m adds a matching all of whose edges have a fresh degree-one endpoint, hence preserves forestness. Every cycle is finite. Theorem E applies with the sparse symbol relabeled 1, using exactly the same zero-based incidence graph. An independent bounded DSU check also matched all 4,495 triples through c=30: initialize 2(c+1) vertices, union i with c+1+t-i for t=a,b,c and 0<=i<=t, and compare the number of unsuccessful unions with the formula. The frozen checker and output were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The finite check is only supplemental; the infinite extension is justified by the forest characterization and the finite-cycle argument.

evidence: Fine–Wilf controls all two-distance interval graphs at or above p+q-gcd(p,q), with no restriction arising from additive supports.

Theorem E characterizes all infinite Abelian pattern Sturmian supports by forestness after symbol exchange. The proof of Proposition 7.14 rules out any cycle whose maximal support sum is larger than twice every smaller sum in the cycle.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Fine–Wilf implies the exact component count for the whole required parameter range above threshold, and the edge count gives zero rank below it by nesting. The prior maximal-edge proof applies unchanged to any cycle involving one of the appended sums, so no restriction on the earlier gaps is needed once the prefix graph is a forest.

evidence: For N≥N0=d+e-g the period graph has g components; E-V+g=N-d-e+g. At N0 this is zero, so all shorter induced interval graphs also have rank zero.

A cycle already present in the prefix cannot disappear. If a cycle involves an appended sum, take its largest sum t. The two adjacent lower-sum edges in that cycle have sums at most the previous maximum m, which would force both endpoint labels of the t-edge to be at most m, impossible since t>2m.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These direct calculations recover both boxed claims for all parameters from prior results, rather than simply matching a numerical case or the paper title.

The existence equivalence then follows from Theorem E and the maximal-edge argument in Proposition 7.14, applied only to cycles using at least one newly appended sum.
